assumptions: p=0.5 maximizes variance, giving a conservative sample size.
Wilson score intervals are used for proportion estimates.
Systematic selection over a stable item_id sort is deterministic.
A sample supports spot-check; it does not certify the whole population.
citations: Cochran, W. G. (1977). Sampling Techniques (3rd ed.). Wiley.
Wilson, E. B. (1927). Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference. JASA, 22(158), 209-212.
disclaimer: Advisory only. Accountable owners remain the source of truth for auto-approval policy and outcomes. This audit sample supports retrospective human spot-check; it does not certify the whole population, and escapes are a lagging signal. All data is synthetic.
sample_size_formula: Cochran n0 = z^2 * p(1-p) / e^2, p=0.5 conservative
selection: per stratum: sort by item_id, stride = ceil(N_h/n_h), pick every stride-th from index 0
